summary: Off-World Odyssey is a kid-friendly interactive 3D guide to abandoned spacecraft on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. Players zoom from a world map down to 15 missions, including Apollo 11, Luna 9, Opportunity, Voyager 1 and New Horizons. They rotate each machine, tap its parts to learn what they do, and watch how it launched and why it stopped working, such as the dust storm that silenced Opportunity. Each mission has a short story with voiceover, a quiz, stars, badges, levels and a printable certificate. It answers “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” by turning retired missions into stories that children can explore and remember. It matters because it builds curiosity about space history and engineering, and it runs in any browser with no install.
details:
Off-World Odyssey is a single-page web app built with JavaScript and Three.js. It runs on a phone or laptop and needs no install.

How it works: you pick the Moon, Mars or Deep Space and zoom into one of 15 missions. Each mission has a 3D model you can spin and tap for part explanations, plus a “find the part” game. A launch scene shows the rocket, its stages and the trip to the destination. A “why it stopped” scene replays the mission’s end with fading signal and power. Each mission also has a narrated story, a three-question quiz, stars, a badge and a level. Progress is saved in the browser, and a certificate can be printed.

Benefits and impact: it makes space history easy for children to understand and gives teachers a free classroom tool. It treats “abandoned” missions as stories worth remembering, not as failures.

Creativity: a Google-Earth-style zoom, storytelling beats tied to animation, and real human voiceover on several missions.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js (WebGL) and the Web Speech API for fallback narration. Models, textures and animations are procedural and made in code. Voiceovers were recorded by a friend. Mission facts come from NASA and other space-agency pages.

Factors considered: child-friendly language and visuals, phone support, and accessibility through captions and text for every story.
